name: PH
description: A measure of water acidity or alkalinity. Most aquatic life thrives in a specific pH range, making it crucial for fish health and biological processes.

name: Total Ammonia
description: A toxic compound produced from fish waste and decaying organic matter. Any levels can be lethal to fish and must be kept as close to zero as possible.

name: Nitrite
description: An intermediate product in the nitrogen cycle, converted from ammonia by beneficial bacteria. Highly toxic to fish and should be maintained at near-zero levels.

name: Nitrate
description: The end product of the nitrogen cycle. Less toxic than ammonia and nitrite, but should be controlled through regular water changes to prevent long-term stress on fish.

name: General Hardness
description: Measures the concentration of dissolved minerals, primarily calcium and magnesium.

name: Carbonate Hardness
description: Measures the water's buffering capacity to resist pH changes.

name: Total Dissolved Solids
description: The total concentration of dissolved substances in water, including minerals, salts, and metals.
